title: Small-object argument in slice-cover lemma uses (unstated) compactness of generators

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In Lemma `lem:cover-conn` ("the slice cover of a connective spectrum is connective"), the slice cover is constructed by an $\omega$-indexed cell-attachment / small-object argument from the generating set $\mathcal G_n=\{G_+\otimes_H N^S S^1: H\subseteq G,\ S\in\mathcal O(H),\ |S|\ge n\}$. The proof then asserts two things at the colimit:

1. "any map $\Sigma^\ell C\to E$ lifts (after finitely many stages) through some $A_t$";
2. $\mathrm{Map}^G(\Sigma^\ell C,A)\to\mathrm{Map}^G(\Sigma^\ell C,E)$ is a weak equivalence, "the defining outcome of the small-object argument".

Both claims require that each source generator $C=\Sigma^\ell C'$ ($C'\in\mathcal G_n$) be **$\omega$-compact**, i.e. $\mathrm{Map}^G(C,-)$ commutes with the sequential colimit $A=\operatorname{colim}_t A_t$. This is in fact true — $C'=G/H_+\wedge S^{\mathbb R\cdot T}$ is a *finite* (hence compact) $G$-spectrum — but the solution never states or invokes compactness. Without it, the $\omega$-indexed (as opposed to transfinite) construction need not converge and the lifting/vanishing statements do not follow.

**To close:** add the observation that every generator in $\mathcal G_n$ is a finite $G$-spectrum, hence $\omega$-compact, so the sequential small-object argument stabilizes and gives the stated mapping-space equivalences. This is a one-sentence fix but is logically required for the construction (and therefore for the existence of the truncation functor $P^{n-1}_{\mathcal O}$ and the convergence theorem that depends on it).
